newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada native group plans Voisey's Bay protest.
newsitem.headline: Canada native group plans Voisey's Bay protest.

text.p: A Canadian aboriginal group said on Tuesday it planned to send protestors to disrupt two construction projects at Inco Ltd's Voisey's Bay nickel project after talks with the company broke down.
The Labrador Inuit Association said about 30 protestors were preparing to go to the mine site in Labrador, Newfoundland and disrupt work on a road and airstrip.
"I have given notice to the company right to the top level that there will be a protest," LIA president William Barbour told reporters after meeting with company officials at a Nain hotel on Tuesday.
"I would think that we will be in there by Thursday," Barbour said.
Officials from Voisey's Bay Nickel Co Ltd declined to comment after the meeting.
Voisey's Bay Nickel is a subsidiary of Toronto-based Inco, the western world's biggest nickel producer.
The LIA lost a court action earlier this year to block construction of the road and airstrip.
At Tuesday's meeting, Barbour said the company rejected the group's request that work stop while an impact benefits agreement is being negotiated.
"From the company they said simply, we're not willing to stop the work," Barbour said.
Voisey's Bay, one of the world's biggest nickel-copper-cobalt deposits, is scheduled to begin producing concentrate in late 1999 and refined nickel by late 2000.
Annual output is forecast at 270 million pounds of nickel when the mine reaches full production in 2001.
